newsitem.title: MEXICO: Promex aims for Afore with AIG.
newsitem.headline: Promex aims for Afore with AIG.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Promex Finamex aims to sign a deal with U.S. insurance firm American International Group Inc to set up a pension fund management firm (Afore), an executive said Wednesday.
"We continue...in talks; I reckon that in 15 days an accord has to be signed," Mauricio Lopez Velasco, director general of the western Mexican banking group, told Reuters.
He declined to give further details, but said "finishing touches" were being put on the amounts to be invested by both parties. The negotiations were at "full steam ahead," he said.
Mexico is due to allow the operation of private-run Afores for the first time in January 1997.

Separately, he said, Promex was hunting out a potential foreign partner in the insurance business. "In insurance, we gave a mandate to an American investment bank this week, and within two or three weeks they will present us with some candidates." Lopez Velasco said in a telephone interview.

Promex Finamex, he said, hopes to close 1996 with 210 bank branches in Mexico, and in 1997 it plans to make greater inroads into the Mexico City market. "We believe that we can reach up to 66 branches by the first half of next year (in the capital). At present we have 20," he said.
